title: PREGO: online mistake detection in PRocedural EGOcentric videos
tldr: Mistakes are open-set, so train only on correct executions: recognize the current action, symbolically predict what should come next, and flag the disagreement.

problem.task: Online one-class mistake detection: decide, as each action ends, whether it was a mistake.

inputs.name: egocentric video stream
inputs.chars: Causal — no future frames, which is what makes this online rather than retrospective.

outputs.name: mistake flag
outputs.chars: From the mismatch between recognized and predicted action.

training.supervision: Only correct executions. No mistake examples at training time.
training.note: The one-class framing is the honest one: you cannot enumerate the ways a procedure can go wrong.

method.intuition: A mistake is a disagreement between what the world did and what the procedure implies it should have done, so build both and compare.
method.backbone: online action recognition + symbolic next-step reasoner

experiments.headline: The first online open-set procedural mistake detector, with two adapted benchmarks released for the setting.

why: Defines the online one-class setting that the rest of the mistake-detection literature now reports against.

title: EgoOops: A Dataset for Mistake Action Detection from Egocentric Videos referring to Procedural Texts
tldr: Some mistakes are invisible without the instructions: you cannot tell salt from sugar by watching. So align the video to the procedural text and classify against it.

problem.task: Mistake action detection in text-following activities, across domains beyond cooking.

inputs.name: procedural text
inputs.chars: The instructions being followed; without them some errors are undecidable.

outputs.name: mistake label + description
outputs.chars: Descriptions, which almost no other mistake dataset provides.

training.supervision: Three annotation types: alignment, mistake labels, and mistake descriptions.
training.note: The ablation showing that the text is necessary is the experiment the whole claim rests on.

method.intuition: Video-only mistake detection has a ceiling set by what is visually distinguishable, and text-following tasks sit above that ceiling.

experiments.headline: Incorporating the procedural text is essential — video-only baselines are substantially worse.

why: Marks the boundary of what perception alone can verify, and why the procedure has to be in the loop.

title: Gazing Into Missteps: Leveraging Eye-Gaze for Unsupervised Mistake Detection in Egocentric Videos of Skilled Human Activities
tldr: When something goes wrong, the eyes go somewhere unexpected. Predict gaze from video, compare it to measured gaze, and detect mistakes with no mistake labels at all.

problem.task: Unsupervised mistake detection from the divergence between observed and predicted eye gaze.

inputs.name: egocentric video
inputs.chars: Skilled activity where hand-eye coordination matters.

inputs.name: measured gaze
inputs.chars: From a tracker; partial trajectories are enough.

outputs.name: mistake score
outputs.chars: Inconsistency between predicted and observed fixations.

training.supervision: No mistake annotations. The auxiliary supervision is gaze completion — predict fixations from video plus partial gaze.
training.note: Gaze completion rather than gaze prediction is the modeling choice that makes the signal usable, since raw gaze prediction is too uncertain.

method.intuition: Attention is a cheaper error signal than semantics. You do not have to know what went wrong to notice that the eyes stopped behaving normally.
method.backbone: gaze completion network over video tokens

experiments.headline: Relative gains up to +14%, +11% and +5% on EPIC-Tent, HoloAssist and IndustReal, matching supervised methods without seeing a single label.

why: The strongest case for widening the sensing axis: the wearable already measures a signal nobody was using.

title: Transparent and Coherent Procedural Mistake Detection
tldr: A mistake detector that cannot explain itself is not deployable, so require a self-dialog rationale. Then measure whether the rationale actually entails the verdict.

problem.task: Classify whether a step was executed successfully, and generate the visual self-dialog rationale that justifies the answer.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.chars: Reformulated to individual frames, which is what makes the rationale checkable.

inputs.name: procedural text
inputs.chars: The step the user was supposed to perform.

outputs.name: rationale
outputs.chars: Self-dialog: questions the model asks itself about the image, and its answers.

training.supervision: Curated frame-level benchmark. VLMs are evaluated off the shelf, then improved by inference-time and fine-tuning methods driven by the new metrics.
training.note: Two automated coherence metrics come from an NLI model checking whether the rationale entails the verdict.

method.intuition: Accuracy alone hides whether a model is right for the right reason, and in a safety-relevant loop that distinction is the whole point.

experiments.headline: VLMs struggle off the shelf. Folding the coherence metrics into inference and fine-tuning improves accuracy and coherence, at a cost in efficiency.

why: Puts transparency on the same axis as accuracy for the verify stage, which is what a professional-domain assistant will be held to.

title: Procedural Mistake Detection via Action Effect Modeling
tldr: Existing detectors watch how the action was performed. Many errors only show up in what it produced, so model the effect frame instead.

problem.task: One-class procedural mistake detection using both execution and outcome.

inputs.name: task prompt
inputs.chars: Task-specific, encoding the intended execution semantics.

outputs.name: mistake score
outputs.chars: One-class setting: trained on correct executions only.

training.supervision: Correct executions only. Symbolic scene graphs and visual grounding supply the effect representation.
training.note: Effect-frame selection is itself learned, based on semantic relevance and visual quality.

method.intuition: A wrong outcome can follow a perfectly normal-looking motion, so a detector that only watches the motion is structurally blind to a whole class of errors.
components: visual grounding + symbolic scene graph fusion

experiments.headline: State of the art on EgoPER and CaptainCook4D under the one-class setting by modeling execution and outcome jointly.

why: The verify-stage counterpart of the object-change axis: what changed matters more than what was done.

title: Vision-Based Mistake Analysis in Procedural Activities: A Review of Advances and Challenges
tldr: The map of the mistake-detection field: what counts as an error, which datasets exist, and why telling a permissible variation from a real mistake is still open.

problem.task: Survey of vision-based detection and prediction of procedural and executional errors.

training.note: Organizes methods by use of procedural structure, supervision level and learning strategy.

method.intuition: The field has no shared definition of a mistake, which is why numbers across papers are not comparable.
components: taxonomy of procedural vs. executional errors
open problems: permissible variation, error propagation, neuro-symbolic and counterfactual directions

why: The fastest way into the mistake-detection literature, and honest about which comparisons do not hold.
